principles.statement: Retry/fallback escalation logic across multiple candidates must cycle through all candidates as attempts increase, never clamp to the last-reached candidate and stay there.
principles.rationale: Confirmed live 2026-09-15: `((attempts - 1) as usize).min(candidates.len() - 1)` in two real background loops (methodology meta-loop, AMT re-expansion loop) meant that once escalation reached the final candidate in a 2-item fallback list, every subsequent retry stayed clamped on that same candidate forever — even though it was the one currently broken (an exhausted API quota) while the other, working candidate (a slower local model) never got retried again. One real gap burned 6 of its 10-attempt budget retrying a guaranteed-fail target.

principles.statement: A clamp-vs-cycle bug in retry logic is easy to miss in code review because both produce 'valid-looking' escalation on the first pass through the candidate list — the defect only manifests after the list is exhausted, which requires enough real retries to observe.
principles.rationale: The bug shipped and ran for an unknown period before being caught by directly reading a live log showing attempt=9 still targeting the same broken candidate as attempt=4 through 8.

heuristics.name: Cycle, Don't Clamp
heuristics.description: When mapping a monotonically increasing attempt counter to a fixed-size candidate list for escalation, use modulo (`% candidates.len()`) rather than `.min(candidates.len() - 1)` unless there is a specific, documented reason the last candidate should be sticky.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any retry/fallback loop with more than one escalation candidate and an attempt counter that can exceed the candidate count.
examples: meta_fallback.order = [bitnet-i2_s, openrouter/free]; attempt 4 onward should alternate between the two, not stick on whichever was reached last.

heuristics.name: Verify Retry Behavior From a Real Multi-Attempt Log
heuristics.description: Don't infer retry/escalation correctness from reading the code alone — pull a real log spanning several retry attempts for one real failure and confirm the actual candidate chosen at each attempt matches the intended escalation pattern.
heuristics.when_to_apply: After writing or reviewing any retry-escalation logic, especially before trusting it under a real, sustained failure condition (e.g. an exhausted API quota).
examples: Read a real boot log showing attempt=9 for one gap; cross-referenced the fallback_model field logged at each attempt against the actual code path to confirm the clamping bug, rather than assuming the code was correct from a first read.

decision_rules.condition: Writing or reviewing code that escalates through a fixed list of fallback candidates as a retry counter increases.
decision_rules.action: Use `(attempts - 1) % candidates.len()` (cycle) as the default; only use a clamp-to-last pattern with an explicit, documented rationale for why sticking is preferred over cycling.
exceptions: The last candidate is deliberately the most expensive/most-likely-to-succeed option and earlier ones are known-inferior — sticking there once reached may be intentional, but this must be a documented decision, not an accident of `.min()`.
